final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response narrows and clarifies the same evidentiary record already considered. That clarification is useful, but it confirms the core audit issue rather than curing it: the affected HR benefits enrollment segment is material under the policy because it is tied to named rollout commitments, and there is no admissible evidence that the limitation has been resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance. A caveated certification narrative may be a more accurate description of the business posture, but it is not enough for compliant or compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not a minor disclosure-quality issue.
remaining_concerns: The HR benefits enrollment gap remains unresolved for a named customer-commitment segment and named launch use case.
There is still no admissible evidence of completed disclosure for that material limitation before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance.
Open legal review leaves the policy predicate unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the separate release-policy requirement for a material limitation.

Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance permit documenting and managing limitations, but they do not override the internal policy requirement to resolve, disclose, or formally accept the risk before launch.
